name: edgar_holdout
description: SEC EDGAR 10-K/10-Q MD&A sections for companies absent from the `edgar` corpus, fetched only to host the fresh grouped holdout's entity-transfer questions (docs/holdout-protocol.md). Same sectors as `edgar`, so they are same-sector distractors for it and vice versa.
license: US SEC public filing system. Fetched at build time, not committed.

_rationale.new_companies_only: No ticker overlaps data/corpora/edgar/manifest.json, so no holdout question on these filings can share a fact, filing or company with any development set.
_rationale.sectors: One or two per existing cluster (tech, retail, airlines, pharma, energy), so the new filings compete with the existing ones as near-duplicates rather than being trivially separable.
_rationale.form_mix: One 10-K and two 10-Qs each: enough periods per company that period disambiguation is still required, at roughly a third of the reading cost of the edgar mix.
_rationale.known_skips: Fetched 2026-10-01: 14 of 24 filings extracted. The extractor found no MD&A in all three GOOGL filings, the AMD, LOW and ALK 10-Qs, or the BMY 10-K. Four that extracted were removed by hand after inspection: both BMY 10-Qs start mid-MD&A (the extractor anchored on a cross-reference to the 10-K's MD&A, losing the executive summary and every revenue discussion); LOW_10-K_2026-01-30 ran past MD&A through Item 8 to the signatures (191k chars), and COP_10-K_2025-12-31 stops mid-way through Income Statement Analysis (23k chars). A truncated or overrun document would turn a parsing defect into a retrieval or answer miss, so both are excluded rather than indexed.
_rationale.pinning: The fetcher selects each company's most recent filings, so a later run picks different ones. The frozen holdout pins its 10 documents by accession and sha256 in data/eval/holdout/fresh_v1_freeze.json; scripts/build_holdout.py audit refuses a corpus that no longer matches.
